# Why Action Retargeting Can't Just Match Pose: Contact Consistency?

> **Current answer:** Due to differences in hand morphology between humans and robots, the same motion may result in completely different contacts. The C2Dex candidate solution involves recovering stable object-side contacts from monocular human videos and explicitly preserving them during retargeting; the post claims this covers 8 real-world tasks, but formal validation and code are still needed.

## Key terms

- Contact Constraint (接触约束)
- Motion Retargeting (动作重定向)
- Whole-Body Teleoperation (全身遥操作)

## Problem and symptoms

- Only matching kinematic poses may result in different contact geometries for human and robot hands.
- Similar action trajectories but unstable or incorrect object-side contacts.

## Environment

- Monocular human video; dexterous hand retargeting; 8 real-world tasks.

## Priority diagnostics

- Evaluate object-side contact preservation separately from pure pose matching.

## Possible causes

- Differences in robot morphology compared to human hands; same pose does not guarantee identical contact geometry.

## Attempts

- First, recover stable object-side contacts, then retarget with contact constraints.

## Effective fixes

- The candidate method explicitly preserves object-side contact during retargeting.
